o10.instructions: Can each outcome that `anchor.statement` requires be checked by inspecting something concrete: a behavior, output, exit status, file, path, value, tool used, or an identified record? Bundled duties, added details, and informal wording do not matter here. Nothing can be inspected for a subjective quality (robust), a label or mode the statement never defines (R7, Mode K), an expected output, approval, or standard whose record the statement does not identify, or a person's say-so with no identified record. A mode the statement defines inline is inspectable. Judge every part the outcome depends on, such as its destination, target, mode, or tier: if any such part is a name the statement never defines, nothing settles compliance, even when the other parts name concrete files or paths.

criteria.no: A required outcome rests on a subjective quality, an undefined label or mode, or an expected output, approval, or standard with no identified record.
criteria.unclear: An outcome is partly concrete, but what to inspect cannot be determined even though nothing is undefined or unrecorded.
criteria.yes: Every required outcome is a concrete behavior, output, file, path, value, tool use, or identified record that can be inspected.

o11.instructions: Could a reviewer decide pass or fail for `anchor.statement` by inspecting a concrete behavior, output, file, path, value, command result, or recorded artifact? A mode, profile, or label is inspectable only when the statement itself defines it (for example 'offline mode (when --offline is set)'); a name the statement never defines (such as Mode K or R7) gives nothing to inspect. A reference to an expected output, approval, or standard is inspectable only when the statement identifies where it is recorded (a named file, path, or list); 'the expected output' or 'after the owner signs off' with no identified record gives nothing to inspect. A subjective quality (robust, clean) gives nothing to inspect. Judge every part the outcome depends on, such as its destination, target, mode, or tier: if any such part is a name the statement never defines, nothing settles compliance, even when the other parts name concrete files or paths. Bundled duties, added details, and informal wording do not matter here.

criteria.yes: The statement names a concrete behavior, output, file, path, value, prohibited content, or identified record whose presence or absence can be checked.
criteria.no: Compliance rests on a subjective quality, a label or mode the statement never defines, or an expected output, approval, or standard with no identified record.
criteria.unclear: A concrete outcome is partly named, but it cannot be told what to inspect even though nothing is undefined or unrecorded.

o12.instructions: Can each outcome that `anchor.statement` requires be checked by inspecting something concrete: a behavior, output, exit status, file, path, value, tool used, or an identified record? Bundled duties, added details, and informal wording do not matter here. Nothing can be inspected for a subjective quality (robust), a label or mode the statement never defines (R7, Mode K), an expected output, approval, or standard whose record the statement does not identify, or a person's say-so with no identified record. A mode the statement defines inline is inspectable. Judge every part the outcome depends on, such as its destination, target, mode, or tier: if any such part is a name the statement never defines, nothing settles compliance, even when the other parts name concrete files or paths.

criteria.yes: Every required outcome, including where it goes and under which condition or mode, is a concrete behavior, output, file, path, value, tool use, or identified record that can be inspected.
criteria.no: A required outcome, or its destination, target, mode, or condition, rests on a subjective quality, an undefined label, or an expected output, approval, or standard with no identified record.
criteria.unclear: An outcome is partly concrete, but what to inspect cannot be determined even though nothing is undefined or unrecorded.

o13.instructions: For each outcome `anchor.statement` requires, could a reviewer locate exactly what to inspect, including where the result should be and under what condition? Concrete: behaviors, outputs, exit statuses, files, paths, values, tools used, identified records, and modes or conditions the statement defines. Not locatable: a subjective quality (robust, clean), a label, tier, mode, or destination the statement never defines (R7, Mode K), an expected output, approval, or standard whose record is not identified, or a person's say-so with no identified record. A single undefined part makes the outcome not locatable even when other parts are concrete. Bundled duties, added details, and informal wording do not matter here.

criteria.yes: A reviewer could locate exactly what to inspect for every required outcome.
criteria.no: Some required outcome depends on a subjective quality, an undefined label, tier, mode, or destination, or an unidentified expected output, approval, or standard.
criteria.unclear: Something concrete is named, but what to inspect cannot be located even though nothing is undefined or unrecorded.
